title: From Precipitation Deficits to Agricultural Stress: Timescale‐Dependent Drought Response in China's Main Grain Region
content:
Abstract

Understanding the response of agricultural drought to meteorological drought across multi-timescales is crucial for drought monitoring and management. However, both the timescale dependence and regional heterogeneity of this linkage have yet to be adequately clarified. Focusing on China's main grain region, we explored the spatiotemporal variability of meteorological drought and its time-lagged influence on agricultural drought at monthly, seasonal, annual, and interannual timescales. Meteorological drought was represented by precipitation anomaly (PA), and agricultural drought was captured by leaf area index anomaly. Using a multi-timescale framework that integrated the estimates of lag time, correlation strength and drought response intensity, we mapped where and at what scales rainfall deficits translate into vegetation stress. Results indicated a clear north-south gradient pattern in PA variability, with distinct spatial distributions across timescales. Meteorological drought propagated to agricultural drought in a timescale-dependent manner, with lag times increasing from 32.8 to 1031.3 days and PA–LAIA correlations strengthening from 0.13 to 0.48 as timescale expand. However, significant PA–LAIA linkages were stronger and covered broader areas at monthly (∼64%) and interannual (∼76.1%) timescales, suggesting widespread vegetation responses to rainfall deficits. They were further classified into three response levels by considering the impact of aridity index. Weak response areas, largely influenced by low temperature, are located in southern and eastern parts of Northeast China and the Inner Mongolia Region (NEC-IMR). Moderate and strong responses occur in northern NEC-IMR and southern Yangtze River Basin at monthly timescale, and in northern NEC-IMR and central Huang-Huai-Hai Region at interannual timescale. These findings highlight the timescale-dependent regulation of drought responses, with implications for guiding drought mitigation and water management.
